title: Cross-tenant privacy-preserving usage mart migration and normalization
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Console usage telemetry currently feeds multiple downstream marts with tenant-level attribution using ad-hoc normalizations. We see inconsistent counts between the tenant-level route mart and the aggregated billing slices due to duplicated synthetic events (QA, load-test traffic), late-arriving ingestion from edge collectors, and divergent schema versions across micro-batches. This ticket scopes a migration to a privacy-preserving canonical mart that normalizes cross-tenant activity, deduplicates synthetic/internal traffic, and supports optional differential-privacy transforms for aggregate exports.
goals: 1) Define canonical schema and normalization rules for Console usage events that are safe for cross-tenant aggregation. 2) Implement ETL steps to deduplicate synthetic/internal events and reconcile late-arriving records. 3) Add a configurable differential-privacy export layer for public or aggregated reporting. 4) Deploy new mart next to existing marts, backfill 90 days, and cutover with rollback plan.
proposed_solution: - Introduce a canonical_usage_event table (parquet/iceberg) with explicit fields: event_id, event_hash, tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, timestamp_utc, processed_time_utc, event_type, invocation_duration_ms, token_count, cost_estimate_cents, ingestion_source, synthetic_flag, schema_version. - Upstream collectors add a deterministic event_hash tag to improve dedupe correctness. - Deduplication: windowed dedupe by event_hash + coalescing late arrivals using processed_time_utc with append-only merges (merge-on-key) and tombstones for retractions. - Normalization rules: unify route naming mapping table, canonicalize model_variant tags, and apply tenant-level attribution heuristics for multi-tenant invocations. - Privacy: provide a transform job that emits DP-protected aggregates (epsilon configurable) using Laplace mechanism at the export stage; raw canonical mart remains access-controlled.
schema_changes: New canonical_usage_event schema (one canonical table). Add tenant_aliases mapping table. Introduce ingestion_metadata partition for processed_time_utc. Add synthetic_flag boolean and source_origin string. Maintain schema_version string for forward compatibility.
migration_plan: 1) Deploy ingestion transform to write canonical_usage_event in append mode alongside existing pipelines (no cutover). 2) Run backfill job for last 90 days to canonical table. 3) Validate counts and key aggregates against existing marts using reconciliation queries (daily totals, per-tenant active routes, 95th latency percentiles). 4) Enable DP export job and run parallel exports to QA S3 bucket. 5) After 7 days of parity, update consumers (billing, console dashboards) to read canonical_usage_event; support a gradual traffic switch. 6) Monitor and rollback plan: maintain read-only copies of previous marts for 48 hours; rollback by switching reads back to prior tables.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical_usage_event exists and is partitioned by date and ingestion_metadata
Deduplication reduces synthetic/internal duplicates by >= 95% in sampled window
Backfilled 90 days with reconciliation discrepancies <= 0.5% for core metrics (total invocations, token_count) across 95% of tenants
DP export produces aggregates with documented epsilon and reproducible noise budget
No dashboard query regresses latency SLOs beyond 10% at 95th percentile
Runbook updated and QA signoff from PM and Security
data_quality_checks: - Daily reconciliation job comparing canonical_usage_event vs existing marts on counts and token sums. - Skyline alerts for sudden >5% delta in per-tenant weekly totals. - Sampling audit: store 1% of raw events to QA bucket to verify dedupe correctness. - Monitor processed_time_utc skew; alert if >1 hour of tail latency for collectors.
observability_and_alerting: Add Prometheus metrics for canonical writer throughput, merge conflict rate, late-arrival backlog (number of events with processed_time_utc > ingestion_time + 1h). Cloudwatch/Sentry hooks for transform failures. Dashboard: Canonical Mart Health with daily parity, DP export noise budget, and partition freshness.
security_and_privacy_notes: Raw canonical_usage_event table is access-restricted to analytics and platform teams only. DP export runs in a separate job; parameters (epsilon) must be documented and require approval. Synthetic_flag is used to automatically filter internal QA traffic; ensure collectors cannot spoof synthetic_flag without proper credentials. KMS keys required for backups.
testing_plan: Unit tests for dedupe logic and schema evolution, integration tests for merge-on-key behavior, staging backfill run on last 14 days, manual spot-checks for top 50 tenants (by volume) validating parity and DP export correctness. Include load test that simulates 5x peak ingestion for 2 hours to validate merge performance.
rollout_and_rollback: - Rollout in 3 phases: shadow write -> consumer read in QA -> gradual production read switch (10% -> 50% -> 100%). - Keep previous marts in read-only mode for 48 hours post-cutover. - Rollback by setting read routing config to previous mart and disabling DP exports. Document required playbook steps in Runbook.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: DP parameters misconfigured producing over-noised aggregates. Mitigation: default conservative epsilon and Security sign-off. Risk: dedupe false-positives removing legitimate duplicates across retries. Mitigation: conservative dedupe TTL window, event_hash constructed from immutable fields only. Risk: performance regression on merges. Mitigation: incremental compaction and limiting backfill concurrency.
